summary: This work presents an invariant-based shortcut (Lewis-Riesenfeld) control scheme to suppress transducer leakage errors in hybrid spin-superconducting quantum systems where a resonator mediates interactions between a GaAs RX spin qubit and a transmon. The optimized pulse protocol achieves iSWAP gate and Bell state preparation with >99% fidelity, reducing leakage probability to 0.01 and demonstrating robustness against decoherence and control errors.
motivation: Hybrid spin-superconducting systems combining long decoherence times of semiconductor spins with fast gates of superconducting qubits suffer from multi-level leakage errors that degrade gate fidelity; a systematic control framework is needed to confine dynamics within the computational subspace.
method: The authors decompose the effective Hamiltonian into computational subspace ($H_\mathrm{sub}$) and leakage ($H_\mathrm{leak}$) contributions, apply Lewis-Riesenfeld invariant theory to design time-dependent Rabi frequency $\Omega(t)$ and detuning $\Delta(t)$ that minimize error sensitivity $q = \eta^2 \sum_k |\int_0^T \langle\psi_0(t)|V(t)|\psi_k(t)\rangle|^2$ via Fourier ansatz with $\nu = 2.27$, and numerically validate against DRAG, counter-diabatic, and LBFGS-GRAPE schemes.
result: The Lewis-Riesenfeld optimized scheme achieves fidelity $>99\%$ for iSWAP operations with leakage probability suppressed to $P_\mathrm{leak} \approx 0.01$ (scaling as $\eta^2$), outperforming $\pi$-pulse and counter-diabatic schemes; Bell state preparation reaches $98\%$ fidelity under simultaneous leakage, decoherence ($T_1^s = 20$ ms, $T_\phi^s = 3$ μs for spin; $T_1^t = T_\phi^t = 60$ μs for transmon), and $±20\%$ control errors with gate time $T = 40$ ns.
